module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1138

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1138](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1138)
- [Va99] Vardi, I., Prime census. (1999).
- [Kum26] Kumrawat, S., [Disproof of Erdős Problem 1138](https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf).

Note that the conjecture has a claimed disproof found at:
https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf,
see the discussion section on the Erdos problems website for more information.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Filter Asymptotics Real Set

namespace Erdos1138

/--
The maximal prime gap below $x$, i.e. $d(x) = \max_{p_n < x}(p_{n+1} - p_n)$, where $p_n$
denotes the $n$-th prime.
-/
noncomputable def sup_primeGap (x : ℝ) : ℕ := (Finset.range (primeCounting' ⌈x⌉₊)).sup primeGap

/--
The filter on $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ corresponding to sending $x \to \infty$ subject to $x/2 < y < x$
-/
abbrev snd_gt_half_fst : Filter (ℝ × ℝ) := atTop.comap Prod.fst ⊓ 𝓟 {p | p.2 ∈ Ioo (p.1 / 2) p.1}

/-- Given a pair $(x,y)$, this is the amount of primes in the interval above $y$, of length
equalling the largest prime gap before $x$, scaled by a constant $C$.
-/
noncomputable def primeCount_Ioc_mul_const (C : ℝ) : (ℝ × ℝ) → ℝ :=
  fun (x, y) ↦ (primeCounting ⌊y + C * sup_primeGap x⌋₊ - primeCounting ⌊y⌋₊)

/--
**Erdős Problem 1138.**
Let $x/2 < y < x$ and $C > 1$. If $d = \max_{p_n < x}(p_{n+1} - p_n)$,
where $p_n$ denotes the $n$-th prime, then is it true that
$$\pi(y + Cd) - \pi(y) \sim \frac{Cd}{\log y}$$?
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/YanYablonovskiy/formal-conjectures/blob/7c134317104d3b98ecc751afbb79ec0adddf8e7c/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1138a.lean#L496"]
theorem erdos_1138 : answer(False) ↔ ∀C > 1,
    primeCount_Ioc_mul_const C ~[snd_gt_half_fst] fun (x, y) ↦
      C * (sup_primeGap x) / Real.log y := by
  sorry

end Erdos1138

findings.description: The module bibliography identifies [Va99] as “Vardi, I., Prime census. (1999).” The original source identified by the cited disproof is instead the multi-author conference booklet Some of Paul's favorite problems, §1.3. This is a reference error only; the mathematical declarations are faithful.
findings.source_evidence: https://sourish-kumrawat.github.io/papers/Erdos_1138.pdf, p. 1, identifies the original source of Question 1.1 as “[2, 1.3]”. Reference [2] on p. 5 is “Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference ‘Paul Erdős and his mathematics’, Budapest, July 1999 (1999).”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Va99] entry with the citation to Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems, the booklet for “Paul Erdős and his mathematics”, Budapest, July 1999; optionally specify §1.3.

reformulations.difference: The source's asymptotic, uniform over real y with x/2 < y < x for each fixed C > 1, is expressed using IsEquivalent along a filter on pairs (x,y).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, eventually along snd_gt_half_fst was proved equivalent to ∃ X, ∀ x ≥ X, ∀ y, x/2 < y → y < x → P(x,y). The filter was proved nontrivial. For C > 1, the comparison term is eventually positive, so IsEquivalent is equivalent to convergence of the ratio to 1. Combining these facts proves the equivalence with the uniform epsilon formulation of the paper's A(C), and hence the full statement with answer(False) is equivalent to ¬∀ C > 1, A(C), precisely Corollary 3.1. Separate Lean checks verify that the helpers give the intended maximum and prime count.
